snippets.title: ESP32 4-Channel Relay Web Server
snippets.summary: Control four relays from any browser with a built-in web page and a small REST API.
snippets.description: Runs a web server on the ESP32 with a responsive control page (4 toggle buttons) and JSON endpoints, so the same relays can be driven from scripts, Home Assistant or curl. Supports active-low relay modules, mDNS (esp32-relay.local) and a non-blocking Wi-Fi watchdog.

libraries.name: WiFi, WebServer, ESPmDNS
libraries.note: Bundled with the Arduino-ESP32 core, nothing to install.

notes: Set WIFI_SSID and WIFI_PASS before uploading.
If your relays turn ON at boot or behave inverted, flip ACTIVE_LOW.
No authentication: keep it on your local network.
Use an opto-isolated relay board and a proper enclosure for mains loads.

snippets.title: OLED Display (SSD1306 128x64 I2C) - Init & Text Print
snippets.summary: Initialize a 0.96" SSD1306 OLED and print text in several sizes with a live counter.
snippets.description: Minimal, portable setup for the popular 128x64 I2C OLED. Shows the initialization sequence, text sizes, cursor handling and the display() push, then updates an uptime counter once per second without blocking.
notes: Address is 0x3C on most modules; a few use 0x3D.
Nothing appears until display.display() is called.
On Arduino Uno the SSD1306 buffer uses about 1 KB of RAM.

snippets.title: I2C LCD 16x2 - Setup & Counter
snippets.summary: Auto-detect the I2C address of a 16x2 character LCD, print text and run a counter.
snippets.description: Works with the common HD44780 LCD + PCF8574 backpack. The sketch scans the bus to find the address (0x27 or 0x3F), initializes the screen and displays a once-per-second counter without leftover characters.
notes: Blank or solid blocks? Turn the contrast potentiometer on the backpack.
The LCD needs 5V; SDA/SCL still work with 3.3V ESP32 boards in most cases (use a level shifter if unsure).
Use lcd->clear() sparingly; it is slow and makes the screen flicker.

snippets.title: Wi-Fi & MQTT Client Boilerplate
snippets.summary: Non-blocking Wi-Fi + MQTT client with auto-reconnect, Last Will, telemetry and a command topic.
snippets.description: A solid starting point for any IoT node: connects to Wi-Fi, keeps an MQTT session alive with exponential backoff, publishes retained online/offline status with a Last Will, sends JSON telemetry every 10 s and reacts to commands on a subscribed topic.

wiring.to: On-board LED (already wired on most boards)

notes: The default broker is a public test server: anyone can read your topics. Use your own broker for real data.
Use WiFiClientSecure and port 8883 for TLS.
Default MQTT packet size is 256 bytes; this sketch raises it to 512 with setBufferSize().
